answer.note: Best match is C, dogwhistle/visibility.py `prepare()` (line 65). It has ARMS = (codeword, public, explicit), so three arms. It picks hidden pairs with eligible_targets, which excludes colliding pairs. It builds trials for every task, arm and replicate. Suggested 60 minutes: C 35 min (prepare, validate_registration, trial_input, the ARMS and REPLICATES constants). D 15 min, because honest.py has a near-identical prepare() but only two arms (codeword, public), so it is the closest sibling and a useful contrast. A (study.py) 5 min: its prepare takes seed and instances and uses regime/condition cells plus an explicit trial, with no replicates. B (heldout.py) 5 min: fixed seed and 30 instances, regime/condition cells, no replicates, and it doesn't check that the eligible list is non-empty. The four handoff_refs files all contain the same neutral text with no file priority. I chose C and D from reading the code only, and I did not run anything.
